messages.content: 印度音樂音階中，C的等效音符是什麼？將頻率440 Hz轉換為波長是多少？

function.name: frequency_to_wavelength
function.description: Converts the frequency of a musical note to its wavelength. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

frequency.description: The frequency in hertz of the musical note. This is a float type value.

function.name: note_conversion_indian
function.description: Converts a note in Western music to Indian classical music. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

note.description: The note in Western musical scale.

message.reasoning:
The user asks two questions:

1) In Indian classical music, what is the equivalent note to C? They want mapping from Western notes to Indian swaras (Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni). For middle C at 261.63Hz corresponds to Sa or something? Actually in Hindustani system, Sa is the tonic; if we set Sa as C then C would be Sa. But maybe they refer to "equivalent" meaning which Swara matches the pitch of C when using same octave reference. Usually Sa can correspond to any pitch depending on raga but typically Sa is mapped to C in many contexts.

But perhaps they'd like answer: C equals Sa (shadja).

2) Convert frequency 440 Hz to wavelength. Use speed of sound ~343 m/s at room temperature (~20°C). Wavelength λ = v / f. So λ ≈ 0.7795 meters. Provide calculation and mention approximate.

We need to use tool frequency_to_wavelength. Let's call it with frequency=440. We'll get result. Then provide explanation.

Also might ask about converting note to Indian classical. There's also second tool note_conversion_indian. We could convert note "C". That will give us the Indian name. Let's try both.

We'll produce output accordingly.
